subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the unit vector perpendicular to both i + j + k and 2i + j + 3k.

mark_split.label: State that a × b is perpendicular to both

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.72, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 23(ii). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+2+1 split rewards naming the construction, the determinant that does the work, and the division that turns a normal vector into a unit vector; it mirrors the split used on the sibling part 23(i) so the pair reads consistently. ANSWER IS DETERMINATE, not a method sketch: the unit vectors are ± (2i − j − k)/√6. VERIFIED: a × b = 2i − j − k dotted with a = (1, 1, 1) gives 2 − 1 − 1 = 0 and dotted with b = (2, 1, 3) gives 4 − 1 − 3 = 0, so it is perpendicular to both; its squared length is 4 + 1 + 1 = 6, so the reported unit vector has squared length 6/6 = 1 exactly. BOTH SIGNS ARE ANSWERS: the two vectors span a plane, and a plane has one unit normal on each side, so the ± is written on the line the student reads, not left to the note. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies at least one of those eight on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would build this unit vector — say why there are two answers.

steps.label: State the construction
steps.margin_note: First mark. The cross product is perpendicular to both vectors by construction, so the whole question is one cross product and one division.
steps.memory_tip: Perpendicular to two given vectors means cross them; make it a unit vector by dividing by its own length.
lines: Let a = i + j + k and b = 2i + j + 3k.
a × b is perpendicular to both a and b.

recall.must_convey: That a × b is perpendicular to both vectors, so the answer is ± (a × b)/|a × b|.

steps.why: A cross product is perpendicular to each of the two vectors that make it, so no other construction is needed. Writing the ± from the start makes it harder to lose at the end.
common_mistakes: Using a·b = 0, which is a test for perpendicular vectors, not a way to build one.
Giving only one of the two directions.

steps.label: Find a × b
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Expand the determinant and then dot the answer with a and with b — both must give 0 before you go on.
steps.memory_tip: The middle term of the expansion carries a minus sign of its own: i(…) − j(…) + k(…).

recall.must_convey: That a × b = 2i − j − k, and that dotting it with a and with b gives 0 each time.

steps.why: The determinant is the whole calculation, and the two dot products check its direction: a cross product that is not perpendicular to both inputs has a sign error in it. They do not test the magnitude, so re-read the determinant for that.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus in front of the j term.
Writing the second row as 2, 1, 3 and the third as 1, 1, 1, which reverses the answer.

steps.label: Divide by the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Divide by √6, not by 6. Both signs are correct because the plane of a and b has one unit normal on each side.
steps.memory_tip: Divide by the square root, never by the sum of squares — and keep both signs.

recall.must_convey: That |a × b| = √6, so the unit vector is ± (2i − j − k)/√6.

steps.why: Dividing by the length leaves a vector of length 1. The check is that 4 + 1 + 1 = 6, so the squared length of the answer is 6/6 = 1, and both signs give length 1.
